issues.legal_issue: The statutory power to acquire the whole land in response to an excessive severance claim applies whether the land is vacant or contains structures.
material_facts: A portion of a larger property was acquired, and the owner claimed damages for severance of the remaining land.
The Government considered the severance claim unreasonable and excessive and ordered acquisition of the whole property before the award.
The property included vacant land as well as structures; the owner argued that the statutory power did not apply to vacant land.
issues.conclusion: The power applies to acquisition of vacant land as well as land containing structures.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(a) of the Land Acquisition Act, land includes benefits arising out of land and things attached to or permanently fastened to the earth. Section 49(2) therefore covers land whether vacant or accompanied by structures. Section 49(1), which gives the owner an option concerning acquisition of part of a house, is distinct from Section 49(2), which gives the Government an option when a severance claim is unreasonable and excessive. State of Bihar v. Kundan Singh concerned Section 49(1) and does not support limiting Section 49(2) to land with a building.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and partial_acquisition and severance_claim_made and government_finds_claim_excessive and whole_land_ordered_before_award

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land.
predicates.partial_acquisition: The acquisition initially covers only part of a larger area belonging to the interested person.
predicates.severance_claim_made: The interested person claims damage because the acquisition severs the acquired land from other land.
predicates.government_finds_claim_excessive: The Government considers the severance claim unreasonable or excessive.
predicates.whole_land_ordered_before_award: Before the award, the Government orders acquisition of the whole land of which the initially acquired portion forms part.

issues.definition: When land is partially acquired, a severance claim is made and found excessive, and the whole land is ordered acquired before the award, the statutory power applies whether the land is vacant or has structures.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for severance satisfies the claim requirement for the power to acquire the whole land even when the interested person also claims other forms of damage.
material_facts: The owner claimed that acquiring the frontage would leave the remaining land landlocked and cause severance damage.
The owner also referred to damage of the kind covered by the provision concerning other effects on property or earnings.
The Court found that the owner had made a severance claim.
issues.conclusion: A claim under the severance-damage clause satisfies the requirement; an additional claim under the other-damage clause does not prevent the power from applying.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49(2) is triggered by a claim under Section 23(1), thirdly, for damage caused by severing the acquired land from the owner's other land. Section 23(1), fourthly, concerns other damage caused by the acquisition. The addition of a claim under the fourth clause makes no difference where a claim under the third clause has been made.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land.
predicates.whole_land_acquisition_considered: The Government considers acquiring the whole land of which the portion initially sought forms part.
predicates.severance_damage_claim_made: The interested person claims damage on the ground that acquiring the portion would sever it from the person's other land.

issues.definition: In a land acquisition proceeding considering acquisition of the whole land, a severance-damage claim satisfies the claim requirement even if the interested person also claims other damage.

issues.legal_issue: Further acquisition in aid of an existing public purpose does not require a separately stated public purpose or a fresh declaration.
material_facts: The Government ordered acquisition of the remaining land after an initial acquisition for a public project.
The further acquisition was made under the statutory procedure addressing an excessive severance claim.
The owner argued that the further acquisition required a new public-purpose declaration.
issues.conclusion: The further acquisition is for public purpose, and no fresh declaration is required.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 49(2) and 49(3) indicate that the public purpose need not be separately stated and that no fresh declaration under Sections 6 to 10 is necessary. Section 49(2) implies public purpose because compensation is payable from public funds; further acquisition under that provision is in aid of the original public purpose.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land.
predicates.further_acquisition_under_special_proced: The Government orders acquisition of additional land under a procedure for responding to an excessive severance claim.
predicates.further_acquisition_in_aid_of_original_p: The additional acquisition supports the public purpose for which the initial acquisition was made.

issues.definition: When additional land is acquired under the special procedure in aid of the original purpose, the acquisition does not require a fresh public-purpose declaration.

issues.legal_issue: The Government need not hear the interested person before forming its opinion that a severance claim is unreasonable or excessive.
material_facts: The Government formed the opinion that the severance claim was unreasonable and excessive and ordered further acquisition.
The owner argued that the owner was entitled to be heard before that order was made.
issues.conclusion: The statutory procedure does not require a hearing before the Government forms that opinion or makes the order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49(2) does not require the Government to form its opinion after hearing the person concerned.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land.
predicates.government_forms_excessiveness_opinion: The Government forms the opinion that a severance claim is unreasonable or excessive.
predicates.statute_does_not_require_prior_hearing: The statutory procedure governing the Government's decision does not require that the interested person be heard beforehand.

issues.definition: When the Government forms an opinion about an excessive severance claim under a procedure that does not require a prior hearing, a prior hearing is not required.
